summary: Stop needless desktop renderer renders. The composer and the closed command palette select only the session fields they show, so a chat streaming in one session does not re-render them for another. agent-store updateStatus, setActiveSession and markSessionRead, and the chat workspace selection, return the state unchanged when nothing changes. App, TerminalWindow, TerminalStrip, KanbanView and CommandPalette select store fields instead of subscribing to a whole store. Sidebar, remote machine, recent session and landing rows show their time through RelativeTimeLabel, which re-renders from one shared minute interval (started by the first label, stopped by the last), so the labels stay current and the rows never read the clock. A dev-only render counter (useRenderCount, window.__sbRenderCounts) measures it and is dropped from production builds.

reactNativeIos.reason: The Expo app has its own stores and components in apps/mobile; none of the changed renderer files or stores are shared with it.

nativeAndroid.reason: The native Android app is Kotlin under apps/android and does not use the React renderer or its zustand stores.

sharedBackendApi.reason: No IPC, WebSocket protocol or backend change; only renderer subscriptions and store reducers change.

storageDataMigration.reason: Nothing stored changes; the store state shapes are the same.

automated: tests/unit/chat-render-isolation.test.ts mounts a real ChatInput and CommandPalette on the real agent store and streams 100 updates into another chat: zero renders. Without the fix it counts 100 for each.
tests/unit/agent-store-noop-writes.test.ts pins that same-value updateStatus, setActiveSession, markSessionRead and chat selection keep the store state object.

tests/unit/relative-time-label.test.ts uses fake timers: two labels share one interval, a minute tick updates both labels without re-rendering their rows, and the interval stops after the last label unmounts.
tests/unit/store-subscription-shape.test.ts fails on any bare useXStore() call in src/renderer and on a sidebar row calling formatRelativeTime.
A scratch jsdom run that mounts the whole App with the real stores recorded render counts before and after; the numbers are in the pull request description.
notExercised: The render counts were taken in jsdom, not in the running Electron app.
A chat split drag still re-renders both chat panels, because ChatWorkspacePanels reads the split ratio; that is left for a later change.
